Key observations from the test image:
- Stems showing dark brown to near-black discoloration at the base/soil line
- Plant material appears dead and dry with dead leaves still attached
- Some orange/reddish coloring on stem base
- No visible white fluffy growth

Top candidates: Phytophthora (dark chocolate-brown stem), Charcoal_Rot (gray/black at base), White_Mold (stem lesions), Sudden_death_syndrome. Let me check reference images.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Dead/dry plants at ground level with stems showing very dark brown to near-black discoloration at the soil line
- Plants fully dead with dried leaves and pods still attached
- No white fluffy growth (rules out White Mold)
- Dark coloration appears to extend from the soil line upward through the stem

**Reference comparison:**
- **Phytophthora**: The top-left reference panel shows dead plants at ground level with dark stem bases — nearly identical field appearance to the test image. Symptom description matches: "dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below soil line upward several nodes; leaves typically stay attached after plant death."
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Reference shows more bleached/gray stems, not the deep dark brown seen here
- **White_Mold**: Would show visible white fluffy growth and black sclerotia — absent here
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Primary indicators are interveinal leaf chlorosis/necrosis, not the pattern seen here
- **Fusarium**: Shows very dark black root rot but different overall plant appearance
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Internal pith browning without the external dark stem lesion progression

The dark chocolate-brown to near-black stem discoloration at and above the soil line with dead plants retaining leaves is the hallmark of Phytophthora root and stem rot.
